titulo: Home, renting and neighbours: Looking for a place and renting it

aula.objetivo: Describe your home and its floors (rooms, ordinal numbers, prepositions of place), look for and rent a flat (alquiler, fianza, gastos, the hundreds) and talk politely to the landlady and the neighbours, reporting faults and asking for repairs.

sessao.titulo: Looking for a place and renting it

blocos.titulo: Asking about the terms and understanding prices
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: ads use impersonal «se»: «Se alquila piso» (flat for rent, literally "flat rents itself"), «Se vende casa» (house for sale). STEP 2: questions to ask: «¿Cuánto es el alquiler?» (How much is the rent?), «¿Los gastos están incluidos?» (Are bills included?), «¿Está amueblado?» (Is it furnished?), «¿Cuántas habitaciones tiene?», «¿Tiene ascensor?», «¿Tiene calefacción?» (heating), «¿Se admiten mascotas?» (Are pets allowed?). STEP 3: to arrange a viewing, use the polite conditional (lesson 29): «Quisiera ver el piso», «¿Cuándo puedo ir a verlo?» — the pronoun attaches to the infinitive: «verlo». STEP 4: about the lease: «¿De cuánto tiempo es el contrato?», «¿Cuánto es la fianza?» (How much is the deposit?), «¿Qué incluye el precio?». STEP 5: English "rent" is a noun AND a verb; Spanish splits them: the noun is «el alquiler», the verb is «alquilar» («alquilo» = I rent). STEP 6: the hundreds complete the numbers from lesson 8: 100 cien (ciento + another number: ciento veinte), 200 doscientos, 300 trescientos, 400 cuatrocientos, 500 quinientos, 600 seiscientos, 700 setecientos, 800 ochocientos, 900 novecientos. 500, 700 and 900 are irregular. Unlike English "four hundred AND fifty" (British), there is no «y» between hundreds and tens: «cuatrocientos cincuenta»; «y» only goes between tens and units: «cuatrocientos cincuenta y cinco». STEP 7: the price: «Son setecientos cincuenta euros al mes» (per month — «al mes», not «por mes» in Spain). STEP 8: «alquilar» works for both the tenant and the owner (to rent and to rent out). The owner is «el propietario» (formal) or «el casero»; the tenant is «el inquilino». In many Latin American countries you'll hear «arrendar» and «el arrendador», and in Mexico «rentar». STEP 9: with «busco» and the features you want, use «con»: «Busco un piso con dos habitaciones y con terraza».
blocos.comparacao: English "rent" is both the noun and the verb; Spanish has «el alquiler» (the rent) and «alquilar» (to rent). British "four hundred AND fifty" has no «y» in Spanish: «cuatrocientos cincuenta». And «se alquila» is the "for rent" of the ads.

tabela.resposta: Son setecientos cincuenta euros al mes.
tabela.traducao: How much is the rent? / It's seven hundred and fifty euros a month.

tabela.resposta: No, la luz y el agua se pagan aparte.
tabela.traducao: Are the bills included? / No, electricity and water are paid separately.

tabela.resposta: Sí, tiene cama, mesa y armarios.
tabela.traducao: Is it furnished? / Yes, it has a bed, a table and wardrobes.

tabela.resposta: Hay que pagar un mes de fianza.
tabela.traducao: How much is the deposit? / You have to pay one month's deposit.
When can I see the flat? / Tomorrow at five.

erros.motivo: «Alquiler» is the noun; «alquilo» is the verb (I rent).
English "rent" is a noun and a verb; in Spanish the verb is «alquilar».
There's only a «y» between tens and units (no British "hundred AND fifty").
Being furnished is a state, so it takes «estar».

blocos.enunciado: Call about an ad out loud: ask to see the flat, ask about the rent, the bills, the deposit and whether it's furnished. Then answer as the person who placed the ad.
Say from memory five rooms and five pieces of furniture, each with a preposition of place.
